blocks.content: Quiz: What does await do when it encounters a promise?
Tap an option below to answer:
It blocks all JavaScript execution until the promise resolves
await pauses the function, not all of JavaScript.
await pauses the function, not all of JavaScript.
It pauses the async function and waits for the promise to resolve
The function pauses, but the rest of JavaScript continues.
The function pauses, but the rest of JavaScript continues.
It converts the promise into a synchronous operation
The operation stays asynchronous, await just makes it look synchronous.
The operation stays asynchronous, await just makes it look synchronous.
It automatically handles errors in the promise
await doesn't handle errors automatically; you need try...catch to do that.
await doesn't handle errors automatically; you need try...catch to do that.
